declared: 2026-10-19 16:05 IST, before any run on real data (built and tested on synthetic worlds only; during this build the real path file was read only for its column schema - the earlier exploratory passes on it are stated under status_of_evidence)
design_history: Drafted 19 Oct 15:20-15:45 IST from Karan's 15:03 spec and his three answers. Changed during synthetic testing (15:45-16:05), before any real run: (1) the planted world showed that the money verdict could be met by the controls alone (a model using only day, volatility and distance sold almost everything and paid, +194.8 bp a trade, because closes in drawdown kept falling there), so the paired check against the controls-only policy (ADDS MONEY) and the controls-alone line were added and ACTIONABLE now needs PAYS + ADDS MONEY + VALID; (2) wording: equal-count calibration bins, the net per trade under the plan and the policy, descriptive splits by engine view, first picks, best rank and test year.
question: Karan, 19 Oct 15:03 IST: after a D or ENS top-3 trade falls 5% below entry, can information available at each close tell (a) whether it gets back to the entry price, (b) whether it still touches +5%, and (c) whether holding to the plan's exit beats selling at the next open - and is the strongest single indicator or the three-indicator combination better? Research only: whether some fallen selections become attractive holding opportunities again, and whether they can be recognised early enough to act profitably. His choices: the money test = hold to the plan's exit versus sell at the next open; a trade is re-assessed at every close while it stays below entry; research first, the watchlist only if something validates.
status_of_evidence: The 2020-2026 history was already used to build and judge D and ENS, and to find the candidate indicators (trade forensics TF_20261019_001 and Claude's exploratory passes of 19 Oct). The walk-forward guards the fitting, the indicator choice inside each fold and the calibration - not the choice of the candidate list. The forward paper trades are the only clean test. Nothing here activates a hold, exit or re-entry rule; D, ENS, the plan's exit, sizing and production are unchanged.

source.run: the trade-forensics run TF_YYYYMMDD_NNN under research2\trade_forensics (the latest by default, or --tf); trade_universe.csv and trade_daily_path.parquet must match that run's outputs.sha256, otherwise STOP
source.trades: D's and ENS's top 3 on every frozen walk-forward signal day (pick_meta's research run, as reconstructed and reconciled by the forensics); status 'ok' trades only (the stuck ones have no exit)
source.market: NIFTY50 and INDIAVIX daily bars from the cache through stage E's loader (regime labels only)

unit.trade: a unique (symbol, entry day): a stock picked by D and ENS on the same signal day is one trade, with both engines and both ranks recorded
unit.repeat: a trade whose stock already had an earlier trade (either engine) still held on this trade's entry day; repeats share price paths - the analysis keeps them and reports a first-picks-only check
unit.dependence: every interval resamples circular blocks of 10 consecutive signal days; all assessments of a trade sit on its signal day, so a trade's repeated assessments move together

event: the first session among 1-4 (entry session = 1) whose low is at or below 95% of the entry price (entry = the open of session 1). A first touch on session 5 is not an event: the plan sells at that close
assessment: every close of sessions d = event session .. 4 at which the close is below the entry price (the trade is in drawdown). Information used: the selection-time ATR14 and the trade's own path and market context through the close of d - nothing later

outcomes.recover_entry: a later session of the window (d+1 .. 5) trades at or above the entry price (its high >= entry)
outcomes.touch_tp5: a later session of the window trades at or above 1.05 x entry
outcomes.hold_on: holding from the assessment to the plan's exit versus selling at the next open: (plan exit price - next sellable open) / entry, in bp. The next sellable open = the open of d+1, or, if that open is locked at the lower band, the first later open that is not (stage E's lower_locked); if none comes before the plan's exit, the sale happens at the plan's exit (difference 0). Both choices pay one exit, so the 35 bp round trip cancels: the difference is net. Positive = holding was better
outcomes.extra_drawdown: descriptive: how far the price went below the assessment close before the plan's exit, as a share of entry (0 if never)

controls.day: the holding-period day d (1-4) as categories. In the 5-session window the time remaining is 5 - d, so the day and the time remaining are one control
controls.volatility: log of ATR14 at selection (atr14_pct from the forensics: the 14-session ATR / the signal close)
controls.distance: z_entry = depth / sqrt(5 - d) and z_tp = (depth + 0.05 / atr14_pct) / sqrt(5 - d), with depth = (entry - close_d) / (atr14_pct x entry): the distance to the entry price and to +5% in ATRs per square root of the sessions left. 'A less damaged close' is therefore part of the controls

candidates.clv: where the close sits in the session's range (0 = low, 1 = high)
candidates.lower_wick: lower wick as a share of the range
candidates.log_vol_ratio: log of the session's volume / the stock's median volume of the 20 sessions before entry
candidates.log_range_ratio: log of the session's range / the stock's normal range before entry
candidates.rel_nifty_cum: the trade so far minus NIFTY since the entry open
candidates.since_event: sessions since the first -5% session (d - event session)
candidates.new_low: the session made the trade's lowest low so far (1/0)
candidates.rule: a candidate missing for more than 5% of the assessments is dropped and reported; then assessments with any missing control or candidate are dropped and counted

combination: the existing three-indicator combination, as a 0-3 score at the assessment close: (close above -5% from entry) + (close in the upper half of the session's range, clv >= 0.5) + (trade so far vs NIFTY at or above the median of the training assessments on the same day d)

models.M1: controls + the strongest single candidate, chosen anew in every fold on training data only: the lowest 5-block cross-validated log-loss (hold_on: mean squared error); if no candidate beats the controls there, M1 = M0 for that fold
models.binary: logistic regression on standardised inputs (scikit-learn, C = 1.0); probabilities recalibrated with a Platt map fitted on the training data's own out-of-fold predictions (5 chronological blocks) - test data never touches a calibrator
models.hold_on: ridge regression (alpha 1.0) on standardised inputs, the target winsorised at the training 1st and 99th percentiles

walk_forward: test years 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 (signal day's year). Training = every assessment of trades whose plan exit came before 1 January of the test year (no outcome overlaps the test year); a fold needs >= 300 training assessments and >= 30 positives per binary outcome, otherwise that outcome is not tested in it. The final models for the prospective test and a later watchlist are fitted the same way on the whole history

evaluation.pooled: out-of-sample predictions of all test years together; D and ENS together with each unique trade once (primary); D, ENS and shared trades, and first picks only, descriptive
evaluation.binary: within-day AUC (pairs compared only on the same holding-period day), log-loss, Brier skill against the training base rate, paired log-loss gains M1 - M0, M2 - M0, M2 - M1, calibration by tenths of the predictions (equal-count bins; expected calibration error, calibration-in-the-large = mean predicted minus observed, slope), recovery signals = calibrated probability at or above the training top-third cut (false signal = a signal that did not recover), all with 95% intervals
evaluation.hold_on: realised mean; each model's rank correlation with it; realised hold_on by tercile of the prediction; a research-only policy that sells at the next open at the first assessment where the predicted hold_on is below 0, against the unchanged baseline (always hold), for M0 (the controls-only policy), M1 and M2, and M1 and M2 each against M0's policy on the same trades: net bp per trade, share of trades sold, false exits (sold although holding would have gained), extra drawdown avoided; and the trade's net per trade under the unchanged plan and under the policy
evaluation.regimes: NIFTY over the 20 sessions before the assessment day up / down; INDIA VIX level in thirds of the assessment days: sample sizes, base rates, within-day AUC, hold_on and the policy - descriptive; the same table by engine (all D picks, all ENS picks, picked by both, D only, ENS only), first picks vs repeats, best rank and test year
evaluation.intervals: circular blocks of 10 signal days, 2,000 resamples (500 for descriptive tables), seed 7

decision_criteria.per binary outcome and model (M1, M2): DISCRIMINATES = within-day AUC lower bound > 0.5; ADDS TO CONTROLS = log-loss gain over M0 lower bound > 0; CALIBRATED = expected calibration error <= 0.05 and |calibration-in-the-large| <= 0.03; VALID = all three
decision_criteria.combination vs single (per outcome): COMBINATION BETTER if the M2 - M1 log-loss gain lower bound > 0; SINGLE BETTER if its upper bound < 0; otherwise NO DIFFERENCE SHOWN
decision_criteria.money (per model M1, M2): PAYS if the research policy beats the baseline with a 95% interval above 0 (bp per trade, trades with at least one assessment); HARMS if below 0; otherwise NOT SHOWN. ADDS MONEY if the model's policy minus the controls-only (M0) policy on the same trades has a 95% interval above 0; LOSES MONEY if below 0; otherwise NOT SHOWN. M0's own policy against the baseline is reported as 'the controls alone' (PAYS / HARMS / NOT SHOWN): if it pays, that is a stop-type rule on the day, volatility and distance, not a recovery-indicator finding, and needs its own declared test
decision_criteria.overall: ACTIONABLE EVIDENCE only if, for the same model, the money verdict is PAYS, it ADDS MONEY over the controls-only policy, and the model is VALID for recover_entry; otherwise INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE TO ACT - stated as such, with the parts that do hold
decision_criteria.watchlist gating (stage 2): an outcome's probability is shown only from a VALID model (M1 unless COMBINATION BETTER and M2 VALID); the hold-on figure only from a model that PAYS and ADDS MONEY; a case with fewer than 30 comparable historical assessments (same day d, z_entry within 0.25) shows 'insufficient comparable cases' and no number

prospective: the final models, frozen with their SHA-256 before any forward day is assessed, applied to the paper test's traded picks (first 3 buyable per engine, on-time watchlists only) from 2026-09-30. Month 6 = signal days through 2027-03-31, month 12 = through 2027-09-30, each judged once when every window position has closed: DISCRIMINATES and CALIBRATED per binary outcome, the money policy against the baseline, with at least 100 assessments and 30 positives per outcome (otherwise NOT ENOUGH EVENTS). Built in stage 2, only if this study finds a VALID model or PAYS.
outputs: research2\recovery_watch\RW_YYYYMMDD_NNN\: report.md, summary.json, assessments.csv (every assessment with its inputs, outcomes and out-of-sample predictions), calibration.csv, folds.csv, regimes.csv, final_models.json, outputs.sha256; ledger lines recovery_watch_declared (first run, with this file's SHA-256) and recovery_watch_run in panel\research_ledger.jsonl. A second study run needs --rerun-reason; a changed declaration is refused.
limits: Same history as the engines and the forensics; the candidate list was suggested by looking at it.
Daily bars: within a session the order of a new low and a recovery is unknown; outcomes count from the next session on.
Selling at the next open is the opening auction at that price (stage E's convention), no extra slippage beyond the 35 bp both choices share.
No survivorship correction (as the engines' research); NIFTY and VIX label the regime, they do not explain it.
